notes: Stored edit with background-belief queries, chosen for relation-property coverage: the new relation has_father carries a role chain (has_father ∘ has_father ⊑ has_paternal_grandfather) and a subproperty (has_father ⊑ child_of), and the two determinate queries use them. Derivability very_unlikely: Leopold is named in the first lines of every biography and the fact follows from no other. Chain query: the bridge (J. S. Bach was C. P. E. Bach's father) is firm, so a directly stored grandfather is dropped by step 3. Worlds: two independent storage choices, each by name or as 'his father': who opposed his 1782 marriage to Constanze Weber (Wikipedia has both forms: Leopold 'strongly opposed'; 'permission for the marriage from his father') and to whom Haydn spoke his 1785 praise (quoted as 'your son is the greatest composer'; Leopold named as the listener). Verifier (round 2) replaced the earlier teacher and childhood-tour queries: their description worlds put C. P. E. Bach in Salzburg teaching the child and on the 1763-66 grand tour, against his firm Berlin court post (1738-1768), so they were not valid worlds. The new description worlds are improbable but consistent (Decision 4): C. P. E. Bach (in Hamburg from 1768, died 1788) could object by letter to an adult son's marriage in 1782 and could visit Vienna in 1785. Side facts that go with the edit itself: Nannerl becomes Wolfgang's half-sister through their mother; dates allow it (C. P. E. Bach, 1714-1788, was 41 at Mozart's birth in Salzburg in 1756). C. P. E. Bach rather than J. C. Bach: J. C. Bach really did coach the young Mozart in London. R2: the Mozart surname hints at Leopold, but no prompt contains its answer. Near query (his mother) is not moved in any world. Not a repeat of literature_arts-0003, which edits Mozart's birthplace.
